thread.text: Find out whether our nightly job will hit the API rate limit, then report to the analyst.
Opened rate limit page · plans and burst allowance

Reading the rate limit page now. Limits are counted per workspace rather than per key, in one minute windows, and a batch call counts once however many items it carries. The Team plan allows six hundred requests a minute with a burst of one hundred, and the page highlights that unused burst does not carry over to the next window.

Our nightly job sends nine hundred requests in its first minute, so on the plan as written it would be throttled for the whole first window. Can the job send fewer calls by batching, and does a batch of fifty really count as one call against the limit? I need that sentence quoted, not paraphrased.

Quoting the page: a batch request is counted as a single request regardless of how many items it contains. Batching the nightly job in groups of fifty turns nine hundred requests into eighteen, which sits far under the six hundred a minute allowance and well inside the burst of one hundred.

thread.text: Now check what happens on a retry, and whether the retries are counted too.
Opened retry policy · back off and counted requests

Retries are counted like any request, and a rejected request still uses its slot. The page recommends exponential backoff with jitter, starting at one second. With eighteen batched calls the job has room for thirty retries in the same minute before it gets near the limit.

Good. So the plan is batching in fifty, backoff with jitter, and an alert if the retry count passes thirty in any minute. Write it up as a short recommendation with the quoted sentence and the numbers, and keep it to what the page actually says.

answer.lead: The nightly job will be throttled as written; batching fixes it.
